title: Higher active-hole masses permit smaller tidal-depth changes in tested ASASSN-14ko binary clocks
abstract: We test how active black-hole mass changes the companion perturbations in two proposed ASASSN-14ko binary clocks. We integrate 120 selected stellar orbits for 19 observer years, with a circular edge-on companion and a leading central relativistic correction. Three active masses are 10, 30 and 71 million solar masses. A track stops at 20 gravitational radii. For the longer binary, 16 of 20 high-mass tracks have timing RMS below 0.5 day and pericentre range below 10 percent of the initial distance. None do at the lowest mass. These are reference scales, not survival limits. One selected high-mass retrograde track has full-passage RMS 0.177 day, weighted RMS 0.168 day at the actual observing cycles, and pericentre range 4.75 percent. A selected low-mass track has smaller timing RMS but a 72 percent distance range. Thus timing scatter alone does not measure stable tidal depth. Mass changes both companion strength and central precession. The earlier one-mass result is not a mass-independent bound. We provide code, aggregate outputs, simulated passages, input hashes and precision checks. We do not fit observed times, detect a binary, model stripping or prove long-term survival. The central correction and sparse geometry grid limit the result.
